name: Nighthawk
caption: A Pennsylvania-based former HIWF World Heavyweight Champion who lost the title to a masked challenger, later teamed as one of The Predators, and feuded openly with the Legion of Pain through the rest of 1998.

tenures.source: Retains the World Heavyweight Championship over Leon Redfield on the promotion's own 10 May 1998 home video, recapped within "Parade of Champions"; loses the title to a masked "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh (revealed as Mr. Shh!) at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); fights Mr. Shh! to a double disqualification at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); wrestles John Drake to a time-limit draw in the "Clash of the Titans II" tournament (17 November 1998); attacks Steve Anderson backstage and disguises himself as a woman to ambush John Drake on "November 20 Friday Fights."

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: several unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Mr. Shh!
caption: A self-declared grand-slam legend who wrestled a title match masked under the ring alias "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh, then unmasked himself on air as HIWF's own returning former World, US, Television, and Cruiserweight champion.

tenures.source: Wrestling masked as "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh, wins the World Heavyweight Championship from Nighthawk at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) with Legion of Pain interference, then unmasks on "Monday Mania" (22 June 1998) as Mr. Shh!, "the only grand-slam winner in HIWF history"; loses a non-title match to James Kira on "June 26 Friday Fights"; retains the World Heavyweight Championship over Nighthawk by double disqualification at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998). HIWF's own retrospective broadcast (9 September 2001) preserves a later title defense: still champion, and by then also described as the owner of the Supreme Wrestling Federation, retains the World Heavyweight Championship over new Silent Assassins recruit Randall Flagg at "Clash of the Titans VI: Class Dismissed" (9 May 2000), countering a second Time Line attempt with a huracanrana through a table.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only (this wing's own gimmick carries an exclamation point where the other carries three h's and no punctuation); no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: "Double V" Vic Valiant
caption: A Prophets of Rage mainstay billed as having "held every title currently available except the World Title," who lost the Television Championship in a title-unification storyline and chased it the rest of 1998.

tenures.source: Defends the Television Championship against The Night Stalker's gauntlet run and loses the title to him at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); wrestles Jay Hawke to a second Television title draw on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998); challenges for the title again at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998) and on "August 5 Superstar Challenge"; challenges Alucard Belmont for the Cruiserweight Championship on "August 5 Superstar Challenge," losing by disqualification after Aero's interference.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: several unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this exact name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Jay Hawke
caption: A Legion of Pain member and one half of the HIWF World Tag Team Champions who spent 1998 chasing the Television Championship, including a pair of draws with Vic Valiant.

tenures.source: One half of the billed HIWF World Tag Team Champions entering "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), where the Legion of Pain wins a six-man tag; wrestles Vic Valiant to a Television title draw on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998) and again at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998), the latter loss ending his own tournament path at "Clash of the Titans II."

name: The Usurper
caption: A Berlin-billed, self-described "favorite little bloodsucker" of the Legion of Pain who held the Cruiserweight Championship four times by his own count before losing it for good in mid-1998.

tenures.source: Enters this record's own window already Cruiserweight Champion, having won the title from El Diablo Rolande on 29 May 1998 (recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights"); retains against Rolande in a rematch on "June 12 Friday Fights"; loses the title to Alucard Belmont on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998); challenges unsuccessfully for it at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); defeats Hellfire in the "Clash of the Titans II" tournament's own first round (17 November 1998) before losing to James Kira in the quarterfinals.

name: "Mike B.S." Michael Pays
caption: A Legion of Pain enforcer who doubled as an HIWF broadcaster, using his own commentary position to needle the promotion's on-air president.

tenures.source: Attacks the fallen World Heavyweight Champion "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh alongside The Usurper at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); appears as a regular color commentator on "August 5 Superstar Challenge," openly siding with the Legion of Pain against President Hawkins on air.

name: Leon Redfield
caption: A Prophets of Rage wrestler and former HIWF World Champion whose own title defense against Nighthawk is recapped on "Parade of Champions" as the promotion's own recent championship history.

tenures.source: Loses to Nighthawk in a falls-count-anywhere World Heavyweight Championship defense on the promotion's own 10 May 1998 home video, recapped within "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); wrestles for the Prophets of Rage in the card's own six-man tag.

name: El Diablo Rolande
caption: A Tijuana-billed former Cruiserweight Champion who traded the title with The Usurper in May 1998 before losing his own rematches through the rest of the year.

tenures.source: Wins the Cruiserweight Championship from The Usurper on 15 May 1998 (recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights"); loses it back to him on 29 May 1998 (also recapped there) and again in a rematch on "June 12 Friday Fights"; challenges Alucard Belmont for the title at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); loses his own HIWF debut match to a debuting Chris Hart on "Monday Mania" (11 August 1998).

name: Alucard Belmont
caption: A London-billed Cruiserweight Champion, managed by Victor Diego, who flirted publicly with joining the Legion of Pain while defending his title through the summer of 1998.

tenures.source: Wins the Cruiserweight Championship from The Usurper on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998); retains against El Diablo Rolande at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); retains against The Usurper at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998), where color commentary flags his own interest in joining the Legion of Pain; retains against Vic Valiant by disqualification on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Aero's interference.

name: Jimmy D. Light
caption: A Halifax-billed Legion of Pain wrestler who ambushed a returning Vic Valiant on live television.

tenures.source: Wrestles for the Legion of Pain in the six-man tag at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); attacks a returning Vic Valiant with a ringside bulldog and a taunting promo at the close of "August 5 Superstar Challenge."

name: Hellfire
caption: An Apocalypse stable member who entered this record's own window already United States Champion, before losing the title in a weapon-assisted upset that July.

tenures.source: Retains the United States Championship over "Foolkiller" Jason Bell in a two-out-of-three-falls match at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); loses the title to Mantua Thunder in a chair-assisted upset at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); enters the sixteen-man "Clash of the Titans II" tournament (17 November 1998), losing to The Usurper in the first round.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: "Foolkiller" Jason Bell
caption: A United States Championship contender who later worked as a color commentator on the promotion's own weekly broadcasts.

tenures.source: Loses a two-out-of-three-falls United States Championship match to Hellfire at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); loses to a returning Tony Sanders at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); appears as color commentator on "November 20 Friday Fights," billed as a Television title contender.

name: The Night Stalker
caption: A multi-time Television Champion who won a promotion-wide gauntlet for his first title shot, later held the World Heavyweight Championship with an ally's help, and lost it back in a rematch that November.

tenures.source: Wins the HIWF Gauntlet, earning a Television Championship match, then wins the title from Vic Valiant at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); retains it through the summer ("June 26 Friday Fights," "July 4 Friday Fights," "Super Bowl of Wrestling II") before losing it to Tony Sanders on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference; by "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) holds the World Heavyweight Championship instead, won from Chris Hart with the Jamaican Stud's help (date and manner not otherwise attested in this collection); is stripped of the Television Championship under a one-title-per-wrestler rule and loses the World Heavyweight Championship back to Chris Hart at that same show; wins a rebound match over James Kira on "November 20 Friday Fights," with a World title rematch against Hart booked for 12 December 1998, outside this collection's own window.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: several unrelated wrestlers on other wings share a close variant of this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Aero
caption: A Seattle-billed Prophets of Rage wrestler, loyal to Vic Valiant through the group's own breakup, whose ringside interference twice cost opponents a title.

tenures.source: Wrestles for the Prophets of Rage in the six-man tag at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), the losing fall coming when The Usurper pins him; challenges The Night Stalker for the Television Championship on "July 10 Friday Fights"; costs Vic Valiant the Cruiserweight Championship with a botched ringside toss on "August 5 Superstar Challenge," then beats Bomb on the same card.

name: Jonas Weah
caption: A Toronto-billed wrestler and former Prophets of Rage member, on a losing streak after Vic Valiant released him from the group.

tenures.source: Loses the opening match of "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) to Serial Killa.

name: Serial Killa
caption: A Cleveland-billed Apocalypse wrestler and former HIWF World Champion.

tenures.source: Wins the opening match of "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) over Jonas Weah; loses to Gino Giavante at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); loses to Diamond Rio in the first round of the "Clash of the Titans II" tournament (17 November 1998).

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: an unrelated wrestler on another wing shares this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Mantua Thunder
caption: A grief-stricken wrestler, drinking heavily since a fellow wrestler's death, who won the United States Championship in a chair-assisted upset and repeatedly interfered in the World title picture that summer.

tenures.source: Interrupts "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998) demanding a match; loses to Bomb at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); wins the United States Championship from Hellfire with a chair at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998), then retains it against James Kira the same night; interferes in the World Heavyweight Championship main event of that same show, attacking both Mr. Shh! and Nighthawk; retains the United States Championship over Vic Valiant on "Monday Mania" (11 August 1998).

name: Bomb
caption: A rookie wrestler from Franklin, Pennsylvania who scored an early win over Mantua Thunder before losing his own gauntlet bid to The Night Stalker.

tenures.source: Beats Mantua Thunder at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); is eliminated from The Night Stalker's Gauntlet run on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998); loses to Aero on "August 5 Superstar Challenge."

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: numerous unrelated wrestlers on other wings carry variants of this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: "The Self-Professed Legend" James Kira
caption: A Boston-billed rising star who scored a career-making non-title upset over Mr. Shh!, chased both the World and United States titles, and reached the semifinals of the Television Championship tournament that November.

tenures.source: Beats Mr. Shh! in a non-title upset on "June 26 Friday Fights," then loudly claims a future World title shot on "Monday Mania" (29 June 1998, recapped within "June 26 Friday Fights"); loses a triangle match at the "Free for All" pre-show (21 July 1998); wins a match at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" to earn a United States title shot, then loses to champion Mantua Thunder later that same show; beats Mike Oakham in the first round and The Usurper in the quarterfinals of the "Clash of the Titans II" tournament, then loses to Tony Sanders in the semifinal (17 November 1998); loses to The Night Stalker on "November 20 Friday Fights."

name: Tony Sanders
caption: An Allentown-billed wrestler who returned to HIWF after an unspecified absence, won the Television Championship from The Night Stalker with Legion of Pain help, and reached the final of the vacant title's own tournament that November.

tenures.source: Returns to HIWF and beats "Foolkiller" Jason Bell at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998); wins the Television Championship from The Night Stalker on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference; receives a tournament bye after a time-limit draw with Jay Hawke, then beats an unnamed opponent and James Kira to reach the "Clash of the Titans II" tournament final (17 November 1998), losing there to a masked "Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier" (Steve Anderson); loses the Television Championship rematch to champion Steve Anderson by count-out on "November 20 Friday Fights," the title not changing hands. Makes his in-ring return to the "new" post-merger HIWF with a win over Harley Davidson, the promotion's own broadcast stating only the result (7 September 2001).

name: "The Working Man" Chris Hart
caption: A Calgary-billed wrestler who debuted with a chair-assisted upset, went on to win the World Heavyweight Championship at least twice by his own count, and held it again at this record's own close.

tenures.source: Debuts on "Monday Mania" (11 August 1998) with a chair-assisted upset over El Diablo Rolande; by "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) is described as a former World Heavyweight Champion who lost the title to The Night Stalker and the Jamaican Stud together (date and manner not otherwise attested in this record) and had also, by his own account, previously beaten Night Stalker for the Television Championship in a non-title match and beaten a brother of the Jamaican Stud for the United States Championship; wins the World Heavyweight Championship back from Night Stalker at "Clash of the Titans II," still holding it as of "November 20/21 Friday Fights," with a rematch against Night Stalker booked for 12 December 1998, outside this record's own window; also billed there, alongside Tony Sanders, as a challenger for the World Tag Team Championship held by The Predators. Resurfaces in the "new" post-merger HIWF's own Intercontinental Championship tournament, reversing a figure-four leglock into an inside cradle to beat Fatal Fury, who attacks him after the bell, tables him, and calls out Tony Sanders for "Clash of the Titans" (7 September 2001).

name: "Stone Cold" Steve Anderson
caption: A Toronto-billed wrestler, styled after a famous "rattlesnake" gimmick, who won the vacant Television Championship wrestling masked as "Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier" and retained it against Legion of Pain interference from Nighthawk.

tenures.source: Wrestling masked as "The Human Death Trap" Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier, wins the sixteen-man tournament for the vacant Television Championship at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), unmasking afterward; is attacked backstage by Nighthawk on "November 20 Friday Fights" and retains the title over Tony Sanders by count-out after voluntarily leaving the ring.

name: "Jamaican Juggalo" the Jamaican Stud
caption: A Kingston-billed, Detroit-based United States Champion, managed by Shaggy 2 Dope, holding the title at this record's own close after an untracked win over Mantua Thunder.

tenures.source: Introduced as reigning United States Champion on "November 20 Friday Fights" (the title's own change of hands from Mantua Thunder is not otherwise attested in this record); retains the title over Mantua Thunder by disqualification after using foreign-object powder on him. Billed simply "The Stud" in the "new" post-merger HIWF, now managed by Christin rather than Shaggy 2 Dope: signs a contract on the reopened promotion's first card, then fires his own former ICP-affiliated crew (billed "aka Violent J and Shaggy 2 Dope") before making the save for a beaten President Hawkins (27 April 2001); eliminated second from the World Heavyweight Title tournament's own bye-round four-way, pinned by El Cholo (27 April 2001); billed HIWF World Champion by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast, on the same show teaming with Johnny Pyro in a losing, DQ-marred challenge for the Insano Boys' World Tag Team Championship, and announced to defend the World Heavyweight Championship against El Cholo at "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record); how or when he won the title is not attested by any document in this record.

name: President J. Adam Hawkins
caption: HIWF's own on-screen president, who rules on title matters, orders rematches, and strips champions who hold more than one title at a time.

tenures.source: Referred to on air across the promotion's summer 1998 broadcasts (e.g. "July 27 Monday Mania"); issues the promotion's own out-of-character press release opening "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), ordering a World Heavyweight Championship rematch and stripping The Night Stalker of the Television Championship under a one-title-per-wrestler rule; is confronted on camera by Mr. Shh! demanding a title match be signed, and refuses.

Reopens the HIWF as "a separate entity" after the Supreme Wrestling Federation, into which the original HIWF had merged in August 2000 to form the Unified Wrestling Federation, folds on 1 April 2001; on air, fires and terminates the contracts of J and Shaggy (billed "aka Violent J and Shaggy 2 Dope") during The Stud's contract signing, then is beaten down by the pair until The Stud makes the save (27 April 2001); by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast has fined and indefinitely suspended debuting wrestler Dutch Dixon for refusing to accept a referee's decision.

name: Scott Ryder
caption: An HIWF interviewer and play-by-play host, physically attacked on air during the World Heavyweight Champion's own unmasking angle.

tenures.source: Interviews the new World Heavyweight Champion on "Monday Mania" (22 June 1998); is dropped with a jumping DDT and has his own microphone taken during the champion's on-air unmasking as Mr. Shh!; hosts the "Free for All" pre-show ahead of "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998).

name: "Firebug" Johnny Pyro
caption: A fire-gimmick wrestler introduced as a Silent Assassins recruiter, who went on to win the World Heavyweight Championship as the sole survivor of the promotion's own 2001 tournament final.

tenures.source: Recruits Randall Flagg into the Silent Assassins ahead of "Clash of the Titans VI" (9 May 2000); opens the "new" HIWF's first card by beating Patrick Weber (27 April 2001); wins the World Heavyweight Title tournament's own bye-round four-way over The Stud, El Cholo and Lance Heimrickh with a fireball to the face of the last man standing (27 April 2001); is billed HIWF World Champion by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast, on the same show teaming with The Stud in a losing, DQ-marred challenge for the Insano Boys' World Tag Team Championship.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Patrick Weber
caption: A Tampa-billed wrestler who lost the new HIWF's opening match, then advanced through the World Title tournament's own first round.

tenures.source: Loses the promotion's own first 2001 card opener to Johnny Pyro by pinfall (27 April 2001); wins a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match over Melvin "Mack" Ebony with a chair-assisted belly-to-belly superplex, after a low blow behind the referee's back (25 May 2001).

name: Jim Floyd
caption: One half of The Elements, an opening-card tag team that won the new HIWF's first tag match by disqualification.

tenures.source: With tag partner Airk Thaughbaer, wins by disqualification over El Cholo and Luke Kinsey after Crusher Zubov interferes and Luke Kinsey strikes the referee with a chair (27 April 2001).

name: Airk Thaughbaer
caption: One half of The Elements, an opening-card tag team that won the new HIWF's first tag match by disqualification.

tenures.source: With tag partner Jim Floyd, wins by disqualification over El Cholo and Luke Kinsey after being shoved from the top rope by the interfering Crusher Zubov and put in the Russian Ankle Lock (27 April 2001).

name: "El Cholo" Juan Vasquez
caption: A Los Angeles-billed wrestler who reached the World Title tournament's own bye-round final and was announced for a title match with The Stud that September.

tenures.source: Wins the new HIWF's opening tag match with partner Luke Kinsey by disqualification (27 April 2001); reaches the final two of the World Heavyweight Title tournament's own bye-round four-way, eliminating The Stud before losing to Johnny Pyro's fireball (27 April 2001); by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast is announced to challenge World Champion The Stud at "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record), and is shown attacking Johnny Pyro's valet Fyre backstage ahead of that announcement.

tenures.note: Debuted in the UWF on 18 March 2006 as a special guest referee's own reputation preceded him after an earlier Gold Rush appearance; won his own in-ring debut match against "Dead End" Derek Martin by pinfall (the City of Angels) after Cornerstones interference backfired when Don't Go There turned the tables on Tom Landis and Daniel Kidd. Challenged Trey DaMann for the UWF Unified Television Championship on 28 April 2007, arriving late and out of gear, then had the match thrown out as a no-contest after swinging his own golf club at DaMann; ridiculed the champion beforehand in a promo as an unworthy opponent.

tenures.source: A member of the promotion's own Establishment faction across its July-August 2002 documents, hanged by The Gremlin with a camera cord on 20 July 2002 and defeated by him in a Texas Death Match at the 16 August 2002 pay-per-view.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

A shared ring name only; no document names both, and the other records belong to other promotions or other years.

name: "Cool Hand" Luke Kinsey
caption: A Syracuse-billed wrestler, formerly a UWF stablemate of El Cholo, who advanced through the new HIWF's World Title tournament by disqualification.

tenures.source: Wins the new HIWF's opening tag match with partner El Cholo by disqualification, striking the referee with a chair himself in the process (27 April 2001); wins a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match over Kano Insano by disqualification after Miss Insano slips Kano a lead pipe (25 May 2001).

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Lance Heimrickh
caption: A Glasgow-billed wrestler who won the new HIWF's intergender main event and reached the World Title tournament's own bye-round four-way.

tenures.source: Pays two masked attackers to injure Johno Insano, then wins the new HIWF's first main event, an intergender tag match, with valet Miss Header over Kano Insano and Miss Insano by pinning Kano with a German suplex he calls the Heimrickh Maneuver (27 April 2001); is the first man eliminated from the World Heavyweight Title tournament's own bye-round four-way, pinned by The Stud after an errant Johnny Pyro enzuigiri (27 April 2001).

name: "The Hero of St. Petersburg" Crusher Zubov
caption: A St. Petersburg-billed wrestler who twice beat Synn in the World Title tournament, the second win by blinding him with flash powder.

tenures.source: Wins a submission match over Synn on the new HIWF's opening card by blinding him with flash powder and forcing a tap-out with the Russian Ankle Lock (27 April 2001); wins the World Heavyweight Title tournament rematch after his own flagbearer strikes a distracted Synn with the Russian flag (25 May 2001).

name: Synn
caption: A Las Vegas-billed wrestler beaten twice by Crusher Zubov in the new HIWF's opening weeks, the second loss by outside interference.

tenures.source: Loses a submission match to Crusher Zubov after being blinded with flash powder (27 April 2001); loses the World Heavyweight Title tournament rematch after Zubov's own flagbearer strikes him with the Russian flag behind the referee's back (25 May 2001).

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Kano Insano
caption: One half of the Insano Boys, HIWF's own World Tag Team Champions by September 2001.

tenures.source: With valet Miss Insano, loses the new HIWF's first main event, an intergender tag match, to Lance Heimrickh and Miss Header (27 April 2001); loses a World Heavyweight Title tournament match to Luke Kinsey by disqualification after Miss Insano slips him a lead pipe (25 May 2001); by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast is, with tag partner Johno Insano, billed World Tag Team Champion, retaining the title over Johnny Pyro and The Stud by disqualification after Pyro throws fire in his face (7 September 2001).

name: Johno Insano
caption: One half of the Insano Boys, HIWF's own World Tag Team Champions by September 2001, and a competitor in the World Title tournament's own first round.

tenures.source: Attacked backstage before the new HIWF's opening card, paid for by Lance Heimrickh, leaving him unable to compete that night (27 April 2001); loses a World Heavyweight Title tournament match to Dementia (25 May 2001); with tag partner Kano Insano is billed World Tag Team Champion by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast.

name: "Mack" Melvin Ebony
caption: A Watts, Idaho-billed wrestler eliminated in the World Title tournament's own first round.

tenures.source: Loses a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match to Patrick Weber, pinned by a belly-to-belly superplex after a low blow behind the referee's back (25 May 2001).

name: Dementia
caption: A wrestler billed from "the darkest areas of human soul" who advanced through the World Title tournament's own first round and later joined a beatdown of a former World Champion.

tenures.source: Wins a first-round World Heavyweight Title tournament match over Johno Insano with an inverted Splash Mountain called the Sanitarium (25 May 2001); in a segment from HIWF's own retrospective broadcast, joins Pagan and Mark Adams in a post-match beatdown of Randall Flagg following "Clash of the Titans VI" (9 May 2000), broken up by the arriving Silent Assassins.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap.

name: Fatal Fury
caption: A wrestler beaten by Chris Hart in the Intercontinental Championship tournament's own opening round, who attacked him after the bell and called out Tony Sanders.

tenures.source: Loses an Intercontinental Championship tournament match to Chris Hart, who reverses a figure-four leglock into an inside cradle; attacks Hart after the bell, then puts him through the broadcast table with a running move called the Furious Fall, and calls out Tony Sanders for "Clash of the Titans" (7 September 2001).

name: "The Subway Vigilante" Dutch Dixon
caption: A debuting wrestler suspended indefinitely by President Hawkins after losing his Intercontinental Championship tournament opener and refusing to accept a fine.

tenures.source: Loses his HIWF debut, an Intercontinental Championship tournament match, to Lenny Getz by a rolling reverse cradle, then strikes referee Ben Cartwright; is fined $5,000 by President Hawkins for the attack, refuses to pay or to wrestle unless the decision is reversed, and is suspended indefinitely and pulled from the tournament as a result (7 September 2001).

name: Lenny Getz
caption: A wrestler who advanced through the Intercontinental Championship tournament's own opening round with a counter that led to his opponent's suspension.

tenures.source: Wins an Intercontinental Championship tournament match over debuting Dutch Dixon, sliding out of an End of the Line attempt into a rolling reverse cradle for the pin (7 September 2001).

name: Harley Davidson
caption: A wrestler beaten by returning veteran Tony Sanders, later added to the Intercontinental Championship tournament in Dutch Dixon's place.

tenures.source: Loses to a returning Tony Sanders; the promotion's own broadcast states only the result (7 September 2001). Named as Dutch Dixon's replacement in the Intercontinental Championship tournament bracket after Dixon's suspension.

name: "The Ageless Stranger" Randall Flagg
caption: A Silent Assassins recruit who challenged for the World Heavyweight Championship at "Clash of the Titans VI" and was beaten off a post-match ambush by his own new stablemates.

tenures.source: Recruited into the Silent Assassins by Johnny Pyro; challenges champion Mr. Shh! for the World Heavyweight Championship at "Clash of the Titans VI: Class Dismissed," nearly winning with the Time Line before Mr. Shh! counters a second attempt with a huracanrana through a table for the pin (9 May 2000); is then beaten down by Pagan, Mark Adams and Dementia until the arriving Silent Assassins clear the ring.

name: Mr. Friday Night
caption: A Silent Assassins member present for the stable's on-air recruitment of Randall Flagg.

tenures.source: Enters alongside the Silent Assassins as Johnny Pyro recruits Randall Flagg into the stable ahead of "Clash of the Titans VI" (9 May 2000).

name: Pagan
caption: A wrestler who joined a post-match beatdown of Randall Flagg, described on air as reforming a stable called the Freebooters with Mark Adams.

tenures.source: With Mark Adams and Dementia, beats down Randall Flagg after "Clash of the Titans VI" (9 May 2000), commentary describing Pagan and Adams as reforming a stable called the Freebooters; the promotion's own retrospective broadcast states Pagan won the World Heavyweight Championship from Mr. Shh! roughly two months later, a title change not otherwise attested in this record.

identity.note: Bare ring-name collision only: unrelated wrestlers on other wings share this name; no operator, host, or roster overlap. HIWF's own retrospective ties this run to the Supreme Wrestling Federation merger period; swf-baltimore-1997's own late-era roster already carries a handler contact address matching HIWF President Hawkins, so a real link between the two wings is plausible but not confirmed by any document held here -- reported, not merged.

name: Mark Adams
caption: A wrestler who joined a post-match beatdown of Randall Flagg, described on air as reforming a stable called the Freebooters with Pagan.

tenures.source: With Pagan and Dementia, beats down Randall Flagg after "Clash of the Titans VI" (9 May 2000), commentary describing Adams and Pagan as reforming a stable called the Freebooters.

name: Miss Header
caption: Lance Heimrickh's valet, who wrestled in and won the new HIWF's first main event.

tenures.source: Accompanies and tags in for Lance Heimrickh in the new HIWF's first main event, an intergender tag match, kicking and low-blowing Miss Insano before Heimrickh pins Kano Insano for the win (27 April 2001).

name: Miss Insano
caption: Kano and Johno Insano's valet, who wrestled in the new HIWF's first main event and slipped Kano a foreign object in the World Title tournament.

tenures.source: Accompanies and tags in for Kano Insano in the new HIWF's first main event, an intergender tag match, losing to Lance Heimrickh and Miss Header (27 April 2001); slips Kano Insano a lead pipe behind the referee's back in his World Heavyweight Title tournament match against Luke Kinsey, resulting in a disqualification (25 May 2001).
